dis-dolgusu.name: Dental Fillings
dis-dolgusu.lead: Removing the decay and rebuilding the tooth with a tooth-colored composite filling.
intro: A dental filling is the material placed to replace tooth structure lost to decay or a fracture. At our clinic, fillings are made with tooth-colored composite material, which is bonded to the tooth and shaped layer by layer.
We remove decay under magnification. This preserves healthy tooth structure, and only the decayed part is taken away. Small and medium-sized fillings are mostly completed in a single visit.

If the decay has reached the nerve, a filling is not enough; in that case, root canal treatment is needed first. At the examination, we decide together with you which treatment is appropriate, using an X-ray.

steps.title: Examination and X-ray
steps.text: The depth of the decay and its closeness to the nerve are assessed.

steps.title: Local anesthesia
steps.text: Where needed, the area is numbed; the aim is for you not to feel pain during the procedure.

steps.title: Removing the decay
steps.text: The decayed tissue is removed under magnification, and sound tissue is preserved.

steps.title: Composite filling
steps.text: Tooth-colored material is placed in layers and hardened with a light.

steps.title: Shaping and polishing
steps.text: The bite is checked and the filling is polished.

forWho: People who notice decay or black spots on a tooth
People who experience sensitivity to hot and cold
Patients whose old amalgam (gray) fillings are breaking or leaking
People with small chips or wear on their front teeth

faqs.question: Does getting a filling hurt?
faqs.answer: Where needed, the procedure is done under local anesthesia, so the aim is for you not to feel pain during the procedure. The effect of the anesthesia wears off within a few hours.

faqs.question: How long does a filling take?
faqs.answer: A small or medium-sized filling on a single tooth usually takes 30–60 minutes. More than one tooth can be treated in the same visit.

faqs.question: When can I eat after a filling?
faqs.answer: Because composite fillings are hardened immediately with light, there is nothing preventing you from eating. However, it is recommended that you wait to eat until the anesthesia has worn off, so you do not bite your lip or cheek.

faqs.question: Should I replace my gray amalgam fillings?
faqs.answer: Replacing amalgam fillings that are intact and not leaking is not always necessary just because of their color. Fillings that are broken, cracked, or have decay beneath them are evaluated at the examination and replaced.

faqs.question: How long does a filling last?
faqs.answer: The lifespan of a filling depends on its size, the position of the tooth, any teeth-clenching habit, and oral care. With regular check-ups, the edges of the filling are monitored.

kanal-tedavisi.name: Root Canal Treatment
kanal-tedavisi.lead: Keeping the tooth in the mouth by cleaning an inflamed or dead tooth nerve and filling the canals.
intro: Root canal treatment is a procedure in which a tooth nerve (pulp) inflamed by decay or trauma is cleaned out and the root canals are filled. The aim is to keep the tooth in the mouth rather than extracting it.

At our clinic, we perform root canal treatments under a dental microscope. The microscope helps in noticing additional canals and cracks that are difficult to see with the naked eye. Where needed, the root structure is examined in three dimensions with the dental tomography (CBCT) scanner in the clinic.
Teeth that have had root canal treatment may become brittle over time; for this reason, protecting the upper part of the tooth with a filling or a crown is planned after the treatment.

steps.title: Diagnosis
steps.text: The condition of the nerve and the root tip is assessed with an X-ray and, if necessary, tomography.

steps.title: Anesthesia and isolation
steps.text: The tooth is numbed, and a rubber dam is placed to keep it protected from saliva.

steps.title: Cleaning the canals
steps.text: Under the microscope, the inflamed tissue is removed, and the canals are shaped and disinfected.

steps.title: Canal filling
steps.text: The canals are sealed with a leak-proof filling material.

steps.title: Restoration
steps.text: The upper part of the tooth is strengthened with a filling or a crown.

forWho: People with toothache that wakes them at night or starts on its own
People whose sensitivity to hot and cold lingers for a long time
People with swelling or an abscess on the gum
People with a tooth that has darkened after a blow
Teeth where a previous root canal treatment has failed (retreatment)

faqs.question: Does root canal treatment hurt?
faqs.answer: The treatment is done under local anesthesia. For a few days after the procedure, there may be mild tenderness when chewing; this is usually controlled with pain relievers.

faqs.question: How many visits does root canal treatment take?
faqs.answer: Many teeth can be completed in a single visit. Two or more visits may be needed in cases of severe inflammation, an abscess, or retreatment.

faqs.question: What is the microscope used for in root canal treatment?
faqs.answer: The microscope magnifies and illuminates the working area. This makes it easier to see additional canals, broken instruments, or cracks, and helps preserve sound tooth structure.

faqs.question: Can't I just have the tooth extracted instead of root canal treatment?
faqs.answer: When a tooth is extracted, a gap is left; neighboring teeth may shift, and an implant or bridge may be needed later. Preserving a tooth that can be saved often requires fewer procedures. The decision is made together at the examination.

faqs.question: Is a crown necessary after root canal treatment?
faqs.answer: Especially for molars, a crown is recommended after root canal treatment to keep the tooth from fracturing. For front teeth and teeth with little structure loss, a filling may be sufficient.

related: What is microscope-assisted root canal treatment?

dis-cekimi.name: Tooth Extraction
dis-cekimi.lead: Planned and controlled removal of teeth that cannot be saved and of impacted wisdom teeth.
intro: Tooth extraction is performed for teeth that are too damaged or broken to be saved, or that cause problems in the mouth. Our priority is to preserve the tooth; extraction is planned when no other treatment option remains.

For impacted or partially impacted wisdom teeth, the tooth's closeness to the nerve canal is examined with the dental tomography (CBCT) scanner in the clinic. In this way, a surgical extraction is planned in advance.
After the extraction, written aftercare instructions are given to help the bleeding stop, the swelling go down, and the wound heal; a follow-up appointment is scheduled if needed.

steps.title: Examination and imaging
steps.text: The root structure and surrounding tissues are assessed with an X-ray or tomography.

steps.title: Local anesthesia
steps.text: The area is numbed; the aim is for you not to feel pain during the procedure.

steps.title: Extraction
steps.text: The tooth is removed in a way that protects the surrounding bone and gum; stitches are placed if necessary.

steps.title: Aftercare instructions
steps.text: Gauze pressure, cold application, eating, and oral care are explained.

forWho: People whose wisdom tooth causes pain, swelling, or recurring infection
People with a broken tooth that cannot be saved
Loose teeth due to advanced gum disease
Patients for whom an extraction is planned as part of orthodontic treatment

faqs.question: Must a wisdom tooth always be extracted?
faqs.answer: No. Wisdom teeth that have fully erupted, can be cleaned, and cause no problems may not need to be extracted. Extraction is recommended if there is pain, recurring infection, decay in the neighboring tooth, or a cyst.

faqs.question: How much swelling happens after a tooth extraction?
faqs.answer: After simple extractions, swelling is mostly mild. After surgical wisdom tooth extractions, swelling increases over the first 2–3 days and then goes down. Cold application and the instructions given make this process easier.

faqs.question: When can I eat after an extraction?
faqs.answer: Once the gauze has been removed and the anesthesia has worn off, warm and soft foods can be eaten. On the first day, hot drinks, straws, and smoking should be avoided.

faqs.question: What is done to replace an extracted tooth?
faqs.answer: Apart from wisdom teeth, the place of an extracted tooth is usually restored with an implant, a bridge, or a denture. The options are evaluated at the examination.

related: Should a wisdom tooth be extracted?

dis-tasi-temizligi.name: Dental Cleaning (Tartar Removal)
dis-tasi-temizligi.lead: Removing plaque and tartar that have hardened on the tooth surface, giving the gums relief.
intro: Tartar forms when bacterial plaque that is not cleaned away hardens over time, and it cannot be removed by brushing. It is among the main causes of bleeding gums, bad breath, and gum recession.

In a tartar removal (scaling) procedure, the tartar is detached from the tooth surface with ultrasonic instruments, and the teeth are then polished to make them smooth. Gum pockets are also measured at the same appointment.
If there are deep pockets under the gum, a deep cleaning (curettage), in which the root surfaces are cleaned, may be planned instead of a standard cleaning.

steps.title: Gum check
steps.text: Gum pockets and bleeding points are checked.

steps.title: Ultrasonic cleaning
steps.text: Tartar is removed with water-cooled ultrasonic tips.

steps.title: Polishing
steps.text: Stains are removed and the surface is smoothed; plaque finds it harder to stick.

steps.title: Care recommendations
steps.text: The use of brushing, dental floss, and interdental brushes is demonstrated.

forWho: People whose gums bleed when brushing
People who experience bad breath
People who see a hard yellow-brown buildup on their teeth
People with tea, coffee, and smoking stains
People who have not had a check-up in more than six months

faqs.question: Does tartar removal damage the teeth?
faqs.answer: When performed correctly by a dentist, the aim is for it not to harm the tooth enamel. The feeling of gaps after a cleaning comes from the spaces that the tartar had been filling being uncovered.

faqs.question: Does tartar removal hurt?
faqs.answer: For most patients, discomfort is mild. Local anesthesia may be applied for patients with high sensitivity or considerable gum inflammation.

faqs.question: How often should I have my teeth cleaned?
faqs.answer: Once or twice a year is sufficient for most people. More frequent check-ups may be recommended for patients with gum disease or those who form tartar quickly.

faqs.question: Why do my gums bleed after the cleaning?
faqs.answer: Inflamed gums may bleed during cleaning. After the tartar is removed, as the inflammation subsides, the bleeding also decreases within a few days.

dis-beyazlatma.name: Teeth Whitening
dis-beyazlatma.lead: Lightening tooth color by a few shades, following an examination and under a dentist's supervision.
intro: Teeth whitening is the lightening of tooth color that has darkened from tea, coffee, smoking, or age, under a dentist's supervision. An examination is done before whitening; if there is decay, a gum problem, or an exposed root surface, these are treated first.

In in-office whitening, the gums are protected and the gel is applied to the teeth by the dentist. In at-home whitening, the gel is used for set periods in custom trays prepared from an impression of your mouth.
Fillings, crowns, and veneers do not change color with whitening. If you have such restorations on your front teeth, color matching after whitening is planned together.

steps.title: Examination and shade recording
steps.text: The starting shade is recorded and suitability is assessed.

steps.title: Dental cleaning
steps.text: If necessary, a cleaning is done first; the gel works more evenly on a clean surface.

steps.title: Whitening
steps.text: Applied in the clinic or at home with custom trays.

steps.title: Follow-up
steps.text: Shade and sensitivity are checked, and care recommendations are given.

forWho: Adults whose teeth have yellowed or darkened over time
People with staining from tea, coffee, and smoking
People who want to lighten the shade of their natural teeth before veneers or crowns

faqs.question: Does teeth whitening damage the teeth?
faqs.answer: Whitening done under a dentist's supervision with gels of an appropriate concentration is applied with the aim of not harming the tooth enamel. Temporary sensitivity may occur; it usually goes away within a few days.

faqs.question: How long does the effect of whitening last?
faqs.answer: The duration varies with diet and habits. Tea, coffee, and smoking cause the color to darken sooner. Touch-up applications can be done with at-home trays.

faqs.question: Can everyone have their teeth whitened?
faqs.answer: Whitening is not recommended during pregnancy and breastfeeding, under the age of 18, or if there is untreated decay or gum disease. Suitability is assessed at the examination.

faqs.question: Will my fillings get whiter too?
faqs.answer: No. Fillings, crowns, and veneers do not change color. Restorations in visible areas may need to be replaced after whitening.

zirkonyum-kaplama.name: Zirconia Crowns
zirkonyum-kaplama.lead: Tooth-colored zirconia crowns and bridges without a metal framework.
intro: A zirconia crown is a type of crown without a metal support, placed over teeth that have lost a lot of structure, have had root canal treatment, or are discolored. Because it transmits light similarly to a natural tooth, it is preferred especially in visible areas.

At our clinic, impressions can be taken digitally with an intraoral scanner; no impression tray or impression material is used. The shade is chosen in daylight, and the crowns are tried in before they are cemented.
A zirconia bridge can also be used to replace missing teeth by taking support from the neighboring teeth. Which option is suitable is determined by the condition of the teeth and gums.

steps.title: Examination and planning
steps.text: The condition of the teeth, gums, and bite is assessed.

steps.title: Tooth preparation
steps.text: The teeth are prepared for the crown under local anesthesia.

steps.title: Digital impression and shade
steps.text: An impression is taken with an intraoral scan, the shade is chosen together, and a temporary crown is placed.

steps.title: Try-in and cementation
steps.text: After fit, shade, and bite are checked, the crowns are cemented.

forWho: Teeth with a large filling or that have broken
Teeth that need strengthening after root canal treatment
People who want to replace old metal-supported crowns
People who want to replace a missing tooth with a bridge

faqs.question: How many days does a zirconia crown take?
faqs.answer: In most cases, it is completed within a few weeks over several appointments, including preparation, impression, and try-in. The time varies with the number of teeth and any additional treatment needed.

faqs.question: What is the difference between zirconia and porcelain (metal-supported) crowns?
faqs.answer: Zirconia has no metal substructure; for this reason, no gray line appears at the gum margin, and its light transmission is closer to that of a natural tooth.

faqs.question: Are the teeth cut down a lot for zirconia crowns?
faqs.answer: For a crown, the tooth needs to be reduced by some amount. The amount is planned according to the type of crown to be used and the condition of the tooth; preserving sound tissue is the priority.

faqs.question: How long does a zirconia crown last?
faqs.answer: Its lifespan depends on oral care, any teeth-clenching habit, and regular check-ups. If you clench your teeth, a night guard may be recommended.

related: Choosing the shade for zirconia crowns

porselen-lamina.name: Porcelain Veneers
porselen-lamina.lead: Thin porcelain or composite shells bonded to the front surface of the front teeth.
intro: A veneer (laminate porcelain) is a thin layer bonded to the front surface of the front teeth. Discoloration, gaps, chips, and differences in shape can be corrected with this method.
Before treatment begins, the smile is planned digitally, and in most cases a trial in the mouth (mock-up) is done. In this way, the result is evaluated together before any work is done on the teeth.

With porcelain veneers, usually very little tissue is removed from the tooth; in some cases, no cutting may be needed at all. Composite veneers, on the other hand, are an alternative shaped directly in the mouth in a single visit.

steps.title: Analysis
steps.text: Face, lip, and tooth proportions are examined with photographs and a digital scan.

steps.title: Smile plan and trial
steps.text: The design is tried in the mouth with a temporary material.

steps.title: Preparation and impression
steps.text: Any minimal preparation needed is done, and a digital impression is taken.

steps.title: Bonding
steps.text: After shade and fit are checked, the veneers are bonded.

forWho: People whose front-tooth discoloration has not lightened with whitening
People with small gaps between their front teeth
People with chipped, worn, or differently shaped front teeth

faqs.question: What is the difference between porcelain veneers and composite veneers?
faqs.answer: Porcelain veneers are prepared in a laboratory, keep their color for a long time, and require several appointments. Composite veneers are made directly in the mouth in a single visit and can be repaired when needed, but they may change color over time.

faqs.question: Are the teeth cut for veneers?
faqs.answer: In most cases, only a very thin preparation of the enamel is done. Depending on the position of the teeth, no cutting may be needed in some cases.

faqs.question: Can I eat once I have veneers?
faqs.answer: Yes. After the veneers are bonded, you continue with normal eating. It is recommended that you avoid biting very hard objects with your front teeth and avoid nail biting.

acil-dis-tedavisi.name: Emergency Dental Care
acil-dis-tedavisi.lead: Same-day evaluation where possible for severe toothache, swelling, a broken tooth, or a lost filling.
intro: Toothache often appears without warning. Our clinic is open until 22:00 on Mondays and Wednesdays, and from 11:00 to 17:00 on Saturdays and Sundays. In an emergency, you can message us on WhatsApp to request a suitable time for that day.

At an emergency appointment, the priority is to bring pain and infection under control. This may be the first stage of a root canal treatment, draining an abscess, temporarily covering a broken tooth, or replacing a lost filling. Permanent treatment is planned afterward.

If there is swelling that grows quickly on the face, difficulty swallowing or breathing, high fever, or bleeding that does not stop, go to the emergency department of the nearest hospital without delay.

steps.title: Message us
steps.text: Send your complaint and, if possible, a photo via WhatsApp.

steps.title: Examination and X-ray
steps.text: The source of the pain is identified.

steps.title: Emergency treatment
steps.text: The aim is to bring the pain and infection under control.

steps.title: Treatment plan
steps.text: Options and appointments for permanent treatment are planned.

forWho: Toothache that wakes you at night or does not go away with pain relievers
Swelling of the gum or face, abscess
A tooth that has broken, shifted, or fallen out after a blow
A lost filling or crown
Pain and difficulty opening the mouth around the wisdom tooth area

faqs.question: Is there a dental clinic open on weekends?
faqs.answer: Our clinic is open from 11:00 to 17:00 on Saturdays and Sundays. We recommend messaging us on WhatsApp to get an appointment time before you come.

faqs.question: Can I see a dentist in the evening?
faqs.answer: We see patients until 22:00 on Mondays and Wednesdays. On the other weekdays, we are open until 19:00.

faqs.question: What can I do until I come in for a toothache?
faqs.answer: You can take a pain reliever that your doctor has recommended or that you have used before without problems, and take care not to chew on the painful side. Do not place aspirin on the tooth, and do not apply heat if there is swelling.

faqs.question: What should I do if a tooth has been knocked out?
faqs.answer: Hold the tooth by the crown, not the root; if it is dirty, rinse it gently with water only; keep it in milk or inside your cheek and come in right away. The earlier the intervention, the greater the chance that the tooth can be put back in place.

related: First aid for acute toothache and broken teeth

takma-dis-protez.name: Dentures (Removable Prosthesis)
takma-dis-protez.lead: Restoring chewing and appearance with removable prostheses when some or all teeth are missing.
intro: Dentures (removable prostheses) are made to replace missing teeth and can be taken out and put back in by the patient. When no teeth remain in the mouth, a complete denture is made; if some teeth are present, a partial denture that takes support from those teeth is made.

For a denture to be used comfortably, the impressions, bite, and arrangement of the teeth need to be planned carefully. At the try-in stage, the color and length of the teeth and their harmony with the face are evaluated together.

A loose complete denture in the lower jaw is a common problem. If there is suitable bone, an implant-supported (implant overdenture) option, in which the denture is attached to a few implants, can also be considered.

steps.title: Examination
steps.text: The remaining teeth, gums, and bone are assessed; if necessary, extractions or fillings are done first.

steps.title: Impressions
steps.text: Impressions of the mouth are taken, and the bite and vertical dimension are recorded.

steps.title: Try-in
steps.text: The teeth are set up in wax and tried in the mouth; color, length, and speech are checked.

steps.title: Delivery and follow-ups
steps.text: The denture is delivered; sore spots and fit are corrected at the check-ups in the first weeks.

forWho: Patients with no teeth remaining in the mouth
Patients with multiple missing teeth for whom fixed treatment is not suitable
Patients whose old denture has loosened, broken, or causes sore spots
Patients whose lower denture moves and who are considering an implant-supported denture

faqs.question: How long does it take to get used to dentures?
faqs.answer: The adjustment period varies from person to person; most patients get used to speaking and chewing within the first few weeks. Sore spots that develop during this time are corrected at the check-ups.

faqs.question: Can I eat with dentures?
faqs.answer: Yes. At first, it is recommended that you chew soft food in small bites, using both sides together. As you get used to them, you move on to normal eating.

faqs.question: Should dentures be taken out at night?
faqs.answer: It is generally recommended that dentures be taken out at night to let the gums rest and kept in a clean container. Your dentist will guide you according to your situation.

faqs.question: Do dentures loosen over time?
faqs.answer: Because the jawbone without teeth changes shape over time, a denture may loosen. In that case, the inner surface of the denture can be refreshed (relined), or a new denture can be planned.

faqs.question: What is the difference with an implant-supported denture?
faqs.answer: In an implant-supported denture, the denture is held on implants placed in the jawbone with a snap-on (stud) or bar system. This may reduce movement of the denture, especially in the lower jaw. Suitability is determined according to the condition of the bone.

related: The adjustment process with removable dentures
